name: IRB Infrastructure Developers Limited
summary: One of India's biggest private highway companies — it builds roads and then collects the toll on them for decades.
about: IRB is a road developer rather than a plain contractor: it wins a concession to build or upgrade a highway, pays for much of it itself, and then earns its money back from toll over an agreed period — typically 15 to 30 years — before handing the road back to the government. That model made it one of the largest private operators of national highway kilometres in India. It has run the Mumbai–Pune Expressway under concession and holds a string of toll roads across western and southern India.
facts: Operates highways under long concessions, earning back its cost through toll.
Has held the tolling concession for the Mumbai–Pune Expressway.
Among the largest private operators of national highway kilometres in India.
